newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. airman arrested for indecency in Okinawa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airman arrested for indecency in Okinawa.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force sergeant has been arrested on indecency and illegal entry charges for allegedly breaking into a woman's apartment in Okinawa, the latest suspected crime by U.S. military personnel in Japan.

Okinawa police spokesman Katsuya Matayoshi said investigators arrested U.S. Air Force Staff Sergeant Danny Matlock, 33, on Wednesday and charged him with indecent exposure as well as breaking and entering.
Matlock was suspected of entering a 28-year-old Okinawan woman's house in Okinawa city shortly after midnight early on Monday, the spokesman said.

"We are shocked by this new incident. The citizens of Okinawa are very worried because there have been many of these kinds of incidents recently. This will increase opposition to the bases," a spokesman for Okinawa city told Reuters.

The incident was another blow to the image of the U.S. military in Japan following the arrest of an American sailor at Yokosuka Naval Base 20 km (15 miles) south of Tokyo earlier this month on suspicion of beating and sexually assaulting his Japanese girlfriend in his quarters.
The September 1995 rape of an Okinawan schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen triggered widespread protests against the huge U.S. military presence on Okinawa.
Okinawa is home to half of the 47,000 U.S. military personnel in Japan and hosts more than 75 percent of all U.S. military facilities in Japan.

The protests forced Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to push through parliament a law to override opposition to extending contracts for private land leased for U.S. military bases on the island.
The U.S. Air Force military police helped Okinawa police in the case, the Japanese police spokesman said.
Kadena U.S. Air Force Base spokesman Chris Ames said Japanese police were handling the case as the airman was living off the base.

"Okinawa police are handling the case... He's been charged with indecent exposure and breaking and entering -- basically trespassing.... The incident occured off-base and the airman concerned lives off base. In those cases the Japanese police handle it," Ames said.
"The commander (of Matlock's Air Force unit) expressed his sincere regrets about this incident," Ames said.
Ames said he could not release Matlock's hometown.
